src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:219-220 (_totalWithdraw re-reads LIVE clientBalances, ignores the Phase-1 snapshot)
findings.description: totalWithdrawal is a two-step commit bounded by a time window, and step 2 executes against a LIVE value instead of the value snapshotted at step 1 - a direct vulnerableWhen hit. _initiateWithdrawal caches `state.balance = balanceOf(client)` and announces it in WithdrawalInitiated; _executeWithdrawal forwards that cached amount, but ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy._totalWithdraw uses it only for `require(amount > 0)` and then sells shares proportional to the live clientBalances[token][client] / totalDeposited at execution time. Any client deposits between Phase 1 and Phase 2 are swept WITHOUT a fresh waiting period, so the executed amount can exceed the publicly announced balance - undermining the 'community protection against rugpulls' purpose stated in the docstring. story-048 makes the divergence window materially worse: the reaction window before execution shrank 24h->6h while the execution window in which live state can drift grew 48h->72h (announced-vs-executed drift horizon now 78h). The function docstring (line 414) was not updated and still documents the old 24h/48h phases.
matchedSignatures: step 2 re-reads live value instead of step-1 snapshot
missingMitigations: executed amount not pinned to the step-1 snapshot (no `min(cached, live)` cap)

findings.lawContext: totalWithdrawal is onlyOwner (Law 3, non-malicious), but the two-phase window exists precisely as a community-visible commitment; executing more than was announced is a non-obvious consequence a competent owner/community would be surprised by. manualReview.description: Weak pattern match (recipient-pinning of a pooled payout) but a real story/spec drift: after story-047, NO client receives its own set-aside any more - every client's buffer share funnels to the single global setAsideBufferRecipient - yet the setAsideBufferSize state-variable docstring still promises a per-client reserve to absorb below-par dips. If the owner intends per-client insulation for more than one client, configuring buffers under the new semantics silently strips that insulation from every client except (at most) the recipient - a Law-3 non-obvious footgun candidate. The implementation IS faithful to story-047's stated intent (global redirect to e.g. stable-staker); the in-code spec is what lags. Loud revert when recipient unset is correctly implemented (not a footgun).
